name: Sered
overview: Sered was a male member of the tribe of Zebulun, identified specifically as a son of Zebulun. He is mentioned among the sons of Israel who journeyed to Egypt, marking his place in the early history of the Israelite people. His descendants are known as the Seredites, a clan within the tribe of Zebulun.
namesAndTitles: The name Sered appears as a proper name in Scripture without an explicit meaning or divine origin indicated. It is simply recorded in Genesis 46:14 as part of the genealogical listing.
familyAndRelationships: Sered is explicitly identified as a son of Zebulun, establishing his familial link within the tribe of Zebulun. Beyond this, Scripture does not record any further family relationships for him.
scriptureSignificance: Sered's significance lies in his role as a progenitor within the tribe of Zebulun, contributing to the genealogical foundation of the Israelite people who migrated to Egypt. His mention in the list of those who went to Egypt connects him to the broader narrative of Israel's early history and God's providential preservation of His covenant people. The identification of the Seredites in Numbers 26:26 further underscores his lasting legacy within the tribal structure of Israel.
